2026-08-10T12:34:35.7479586Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7479957Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7480263Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7486282Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7486749Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7487270Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7488821Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7491080Z >
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7493363Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7495727Z >
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7496516Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7497259Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7497430Z ### How to Use
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7497689Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7498378Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7499088Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7499262Z ```bash
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7499792Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7500766Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7501378Z ```
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7501574Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7501839Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7502354Z ```bash
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7502877Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7503634Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7504440Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7505150Z ```
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7505349Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7505950Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7506783Z ```bash
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7507332Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7507989Z ```
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7508177Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7508488Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7509195Z ```bash
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7509701Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7510956Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7511663Z ```
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7511870Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7512126Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7512541Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7513916Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7515453Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7515618Z ```bash
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7516047Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7516888Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7517681Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7517982Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7518455Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7519428Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7527348Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7527844Z ```
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7528047Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7528786Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7529698Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7529860Z ```bash
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7530827Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7531741Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7532450Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7532875Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7533273Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7534058Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7534589Z ```
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7534782Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7534988Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7535786Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7536742Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7539056Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7540111Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7541491Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7542039Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7542204Z ### Notes
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7542417Z 
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7543034Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7544424Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7545642Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7546894Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7548077Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7549207Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7551933Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-10T12:34:35.7552693Z </mcp-clis>
